ca_main_area_5.blurb: The busiest face on Buck's Bar Dome, in the Cosumnes River Gorge near Placerville, in the Sierra foothills at roughly 1,700 feet. It holds 22 climbs, about half top-rope and nearly half trad leads, plus a single aid line. Most are short granite cracks and faces, with grades running from easy fifth class through the 5.10s and a handful of harder 5.11 to 5.13 lines. It works well for learning crack technique or setting up top-ropes, and the dome tends to be shady on a hot afternoon. The river is close by for a cool-off after climbing.

ca_right_side_8.blurb: The right-hand wall of Mayhem Cove, in Eagle Creek Canyon above Emerald Bay on Lake Tahoe's west shore, at about 6,750 feet. All 22 routes are bolted sport lines on granite, ranging from vertical faces to steeper ground off a slanting slab and a cave. The grades start at 5.10 and climb steadily: roughly equal numbers sit in the 5.10, 5.11, 5.12 and 5.13 ranges, so it suits strong leads more than first-timers. It faces east and falls into shade a little later than the cove's left side, and the views over the lake are a bonus.

ca_pacific_street_wall.blurb: A roadside bouldering wall in Rocklin's Deer Creek Park, an old granite quarry east of Sacramento along the I-80 corridor, at around 250 feet elevation. The wall stands about 15 feet tall, faces the street and stays shaded for most of the day, which helps on warm Central Valley days. It has 22 problems, a good spread of V0 to V5 with a cluster around V3, plus a few much harder lines up to V9. It is among the easiest boulders to reach in the valley, though expect street noise and some litter.

ca_birthday_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in Buttermilk Country west of Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra at about 6,400 feet, within the Buttermilks' busiest zone. It has 22 problems on compact rock about 15 to 20 feet tall, mixing slabs, steep roofs and technical sequences. Most lines fall between V0 and V3 with one easier warm-up, which makes it a friendly place for newer boulderers, while a few serious projects reach V6 to V9. The boulders sit only a short stroll from the upper parking loop, so the scene is social and the walk is almost nothing. Bring several pads.

ca_west_face_center.blurb: The middle section of the west face of Medlicott Dome, a granite dome in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, near 9,700 feet. Of its 22 climbs, 17 are trad, three are top-rope and two are sport, and many are multi-pitch lines up the face. The grades centre on 5.8 to 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s and one 5.12. Expect face climbing on knobs and thin holds, where protection can be sparse and some pitches feel bold. The west-facing wall falls into cool shadow in the afternoon, so an afternoon start is pleasant.

ca_e_south_face.blurb: A broad granite slab on Fresno Dome, on the western slope of the southern Sierra above Oakhurst at roughly 7,300 feet. The 22 routes are a mix of trad (about half), sport and a couple of top-ropes, many of them multi-pitch lines of two to six pitches. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12 and bunch up around 5.10, with another group at 5.9. Climbing means friction slab, knobs and the occasional crack, and the older lines can feel runout. The dome sees fewer crowds than the Yosemite classics, and the elevation keeps summers fairly mild.
